    <bpmn:task id="Task_Assemble_Chainsaw" name="Assemble chainsaw"/>

    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_Order_To_Arrived" sourceRef="Task_Order_Parts" targetRef="Event_Parts_Arrived"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_Arrived_To_Inspect" sourceRef="Event_Parts_Arrived" targetRef="Task_Inspect_Parts"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_Inspect_To_Assemble" sourceRef="Task_Inspect_Parts" targetRef="Task_Assemble_Chainsaw"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_Assemble_To_Join" sourceRef="Task_Assemble_Chainsaw" targetRef="Gateway_Production_Join"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_Update_To_Join" sourceRef="Task_Send_Production_Update" targetRef="Gateway_Production_Join"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_Join_To_Send_First_Saw" sourceRef="Gateway_Production_Join" targetRef="Task_Send_First_Saw"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_Send_First_Saw_To_Feedback" sourceRef="Task_Send_First_Saw" targetRef="Event_Customer_Feedback_Received"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_Feedback_To_Decision" sourceRef="Event_Customer_Feedback_Received" targetRef="Gateway_Customer_Likes_Saw"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_Liked" name="Yes" sourceRef="Gateway_Customer_Likes_Saw" targetRef="Task_Produce_Remaining_Saws">
      <bpmn:conditionExpression xsi:type="bpmn:tFormalExpression">${customerLikesSaw == true}</bpmn:conditionExpression>
    </bpmn:sequenceFlow>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_Not_Liked" name="No" sourceRef="Gateway_Customer_Likes_Saw" targetRef="EndEvent_Order_Not_Continued"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_Remaining_To_End" sourceRef="Task_Produce_Remaining_Saws" targetRef="EndEvent_Order_Completed"/>

rules.instruction: When the description states that a participant first has to identify or decide which of several items they want, as a preparatory step before further work on those items begins: Model that identification as a user task on the sequence flow directly after the process start event and before the first step that depends on the chosen items. Do not omit it, and do not model it as a second start event that stands beside the process start.
rules.situation: the description says a participant must first receive the defining details of an item from another party, and only after those details are known does the participant start several parallel procurement or production actions that depend on them

rules.instruction: When the description states that an external party (such as a customer) supplies the requirements or properties of an order, and that parallel work on the order starts only after those requirements are known: Model the act of receiving those requirements as a bpmn:userTask placed on the sequence flow after the process start event and before the parallel gateway that splits the work. Do not make the receipt of the requirements the start event itself, and do not omit the task.
rules.situation: the description states that an external party (such as a customer) supplies the requirements or properties of an order, and that parallel work on the order starts only after those requirements are known

rules.instruction: When the description names a step with a specific verb and object, and the candidate task label would replace that verb or object with a synonym: When the description states a step with a verb and object, name the task with that same verb and object, keeping the description's word choice. Do not swap in a synonym that changes the verb, because the paraphrase can drift from what the description says the step does.
rules.situation: the description states an action whose object is a constituent item that is later combined into a larger item being built, and the description names that constituent item as the object of the action

rules.instruction: When the description states a participant's sequence of actions (an initial request or search, then a choice among options, then entry of further information or payment), each described as a separate step before a system step that depends on them: Model each stated participant action as its own user task, in the order the description gives, including the opening request or search that starts the process. Connect these tasks in sequence before the system task that depends on them. Do not omit a stated action because it appears only as a clause within a sentence, and do not fold several stated actions into one task.
rules.situation: the description states a step that a person performs by hand on delivered or produced items, such as a manual check or inspection, placed between a waiting step and a later assembly or production step, and the description also states that a produced result is handed to an outside party

rules.instruction: When the description says that after a party supplies information, the modeled participant starts an action on several parallel paths, and the result of that action is awaited or checked later: Model each started action as its own task on its parallel branch, placed between the fork gateway and the join gateway that synchronizes the branches. Model the later arrival or check of the result as a separate step after that task, such as an intermediate catch event or a check task. Do not let the arrival event replace the action task.
rules.situation: the description says that after a party supplies information, the modeled participant starts an action on several parallel paths, and the result of that action is awaited or checked later
